title: Use a clock-skew-safe timestamp, not client clock, for notification_settings updated_at LWW field
why: This client-computed timestamp becomes the payload's updated_at field pushed via enqueueNotificationSettings; core/sync/merge/notification_settings_merger.dart (outside this batch) parses remote['updated_at'] to arbitrate LWW. If two devices' clocks disagree, the device with the faster/wrong clock can push a stale settings change that looks 'newer' and wins over a genuinely newer change made on a correctly-clocked device, silently reverting the user's real edit with no error surfaced anywhere. Confirming the full blast radius requires reading the outbox-drain write path (outside this batch) to see whether it overwrites this field with FieldValue.serverTimestamp() before commit.
recommendation: Confirm whether the write path already substitutes a server timestamp before commit; if not, do so, or route the push side through the same clock-skew arbitration MergeStore.remoteIsNewer already implements for the pull side.
acceptance_criteria: A sync test with an artificially-skewed local clock demonstrates the genuinely later settings write wins regardless of which device has the faster clock.

corrections: DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() confirmed to be raw SystemLocalDayClock (core/utils/date_utils.dart:15-19) — genuinely uncorrected client clock, strengthening the claim.
